newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen down on Sakakibara rate comments.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen down on Sakakibara rate comments.

text.p: The key December Euroyen futures contract was down in late-morning Tokyo in response to comments by a senior Finance Ministry official overnight.

Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the ministry's International Finance Bureau, said on Wednesday that although monetary policy was in the hands of the Bank of Japan, there was political pressure to raise the official discount rate.

"Some politicians have called for a rise in the official discount rate. It is true that there is an atmosphere among politicians to raise the official discount rate," he told currency dealers at a foreign exchange conference.

A foreign media report quoted a forex dealer who attended the conference as saying that Sakakibara said Japan would consider raising interest rates from June through August, after examining economic indicators for April to June.
"The media report knocked down December (Euroyen) at the outset as it reignited fears of a credit tightening," said a European bank trader.

Sentiment was depressed further as the Bank of Japan (BOJ) let the bank reserve fall to a surplus of around 90 billion yen on Thursday through its regular money market operation, from 200 bilion yen on Wednesday.
The December contract recovered some ground by midday, supported by heavy bids placed at 99.06-99.07, traders said.
December Euroyen stood at 99.10 at noon compared with 99.13 at Wedneday's close.
In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, a U.S. investment bank paid a seven-year fixed interest rate in a small-lot deal.
This, along with rises in JGB yields across the curve, pushed up IRS rates and induced hedge selling in the Euroyen futures market, traders said.
